pageCache.pageTitle: The Willows School and Early Years Centre:
pageCache.text:
Student Login
To become honest active citizens and lifelong learners in a global society
Welcome to The Willows School and Early Years Centre. Let me start by saying that I have the unique privilage of being the Headteacher of this amazing school and everyday I get to work with dedicated staff, children, families and Governors. We consider ourselves to be in a fortunate position working within such a diverse community alongside many inspiring people. I do hope that you find our website informative and useful.
We are an excellent infant school providing care and education for children aged 2 to 7 years old. We work closely with Pebbles Children’s Centre and other agencies. We are a friendly, nurturing school and aim to work in partnership with parents and carers to provide an excellent education in a secure, stimulating environment. We offer an exciting and creative curriculum where the children have fun and become passionate learners. We are dedicated to offering a broad curriculum which includes as many real life experiences as possible.
We hope that your children will be very happy with us and we understand that every child is unique. We look carefully at all their individual needs as soon as they begin their Learning Journey with us. We have a large and experienced staff team who not only educate but also nurture and care for your children. The staff and Governors are committed to both the children and families and truly believe that together we can make a difference to the whole community. Visits are warmly welcomed, please ring or come to the school office to make an appointment.
We do have a wrap around which extends the school day from 8.00am until 6.00pm. Please see the information about breakfast club and 3-2-6 clubs for how to book and costings.
Our school day times are as follows:main school (reception, year 1 and 2) will have their doors open at 8.35am, register at 8.45am to start the school day. The doors will open at 3.15pm at the end of the school day. This is total of 32.5 hours per week school time. (main gates open at 8.30 am and again at 2.55pm)
Nursery school day will run from doors open at 8.35am, register at 8.45am until 11.45am for a morning session or 3.00pm for a full day session. If your child only attends in the afternoon they will have doors open at 11.55am, register at 12.00noon and finish at 3.00pm.
Mrs Jo Orbell-Headteacher

pageCache.text:
Student Login
Pebbles Children Centre
Pebbles Children Centre is a place you can come to with your child and have fun! All our sessions are available for all children, parents, carers and guardians. We have lots of exciting and fun play experiences for your child to enjoy, all which are planned to stimulate their development and help them mix with children of their own age.
Sessions run at Pebbles Children's Centre and other nearby locations, see our activity calendar to find out more. There are also adult training courses to support your own personal development and to support you in your parenting role. Services are available from Monday to Friday 8.30am- 4.30pm (4.00pm on a Friday)
Our Health Visiting team run sessions and work alongside us to support babies and children from birth to five years enabling us to support all families within our reach area. Our reach area covers Fishermead, Oldbrook North, Springfield, Monkston, Monkston Park, Kents Hill and Woughton on the Green.
We are very proud to have been judged as providing an outstanding service for all of our community in March 2011 by Ofsted. Click here to read our Ofsted report. We believe that this reflects how working together with our families and partner agencies achieves outstanding outcomes for all and most importantly our children are given the best start in life.
Please Call Pebbles 01908 240556 for any further information Email:pebbles.childrenscentre@milton-keynes.gov.uk

pageCache.pageTitle: The Willows School and Early Years Centre: Governors
pageCache.text:
Student Login
Governors
The governing body works with the headteacher and the staff at the school to make sure that the school provides a good quality of education for all its pupils. Governors work in partnership with the headteacher to set the strategic direction of the school.
Governors have three main roles:
to provide strategic direction for the schoolto act as a critical friend to the headteacherto ensure accountabilitySchool governors have legal duties powers and responsibilities. They work together, they cannot act individually and they are appointed for four years.
The Governing Body consists of:
Elected parents Elected staffLocal council representativesParent governors bring the views of parents to the Governing Body but they speak as individuals at meetings.
Copies of minutes of governors’ meetings are available in the school office.
School Governors as of September 2025
Chairperson: Mrs Vicky Pannell (Chair of Governors)
Vice Chair: Miss Cath Broadhead
Members: Miss Julie Kemp, Mrs Cassie Larcombe, Mr Jeremy Rawlings, Mrs Haylie Broughton and Miss Terri Maddigan.
Ex-officio: Mrs Jo Orbell
Clerk to the Governing Body: Floare-Daniela Ciripan
For further information and details on attendance please see attached files.
As a school we recognise that a diversity of thought, voice and perspective is essential to good governance and effective running of our school. We regularly collect diversity information from our governors which may then be used to target recruitment to address experience and diversity, develop and adapt board practices to ensure inclusivity, prioritise training and awareness and to address any potential blind spots on current and upcoming opportunities, challenges and risks.However we are unable to publish this data as it would mean that individuals could be disadvantaged due to the size of the governing board.

pageCache.text:

Nursery Wrap Around
Our Spiders Class is for children aged 2-3 years.
Our Nursery is for children aged 3-4 years (up until they start school).
Spiders' morning sessions run from 8.45am to 11.45am and afternoon sessions 12.30-3.15pm. Nursery morning sessions run from 8.45am to 11.45am and our afternoon sessions 12.00-3.00pm. Parents entitled to the 30 hour sessions can apply for extra sessions. Sessions can also be paid for in advance if you are not eligible but places are limited.
Find out more from the MKC site: https://www.milton-keynes.gov.uk/children-young-people-families/30-free-childcare-information
For those parents/carers who need additional childcare children can come along to breakfast club and 3-2-6 club if they are settled and ready for longer days.
Come along to the office to find out more information and we will be pleased to help.

Curriculum
The National Curriculum
The national curriculum sets out the programmes of study and attainment targets for all subjects at key stages 1 to 4. All local-authority-maintained schools in England must teach these programmes of study. The majority of this national curriculum was introduced in September 2014, with English and maths coming into force for all year groups from September 2016. At the Willows we plan children's learning through topics. We take children's interests and experiences into consideration when planning and aim to excite and enthuse children in their learning. Creative, hands on learning is enjoyed by all children and adults!

pageCache.text:
Student Login
The school Curriculum at The Willows
We follow our handwriting scheme from nursery up to year 2. Children read books matched to their phonological ability both in school and at home. They are also encouraged to read a variety of texts to increase their love of reading. At school we have core books in each year group which to children share, read and enjoy.
We follow the DFE validated phonics teaching programme Super Sonic Phonic Friends which gives us flexibility to plan according to children's needs and enables us to match reading books to the children's phonic capability. In the files there is a progression chart showing the order in which sounds are taught. Our teachers plan their own maths teaching, supported from schemes alongside their strong subject knowledge to successfully teach the key skills in this area.
We have devised a progressive curriculum to enable planning, sequences and ensure progression of skills and knowledge across all core and foundation subjects. We use Whiterose maths and Charanga to support maths and music across the school.
